Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:109703
Court No. - 76

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 10797 of 2023
Applicant :- Zeeshan

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Anil Kumar Singh,Raj Kumar Ojha
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anup Kumar Khare
Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
1.

Counter affidavit filed on behalf of Informant is without the direction of this Court, therefore, the
same is returned back.

2. Heard Sri Raj Kumar Ojha, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Markandey Singh, learned Brief Holder for State and Sri Arvind Singh, Advocate holding brief of Sri Anup Kumar Khare, Advocate for Informant.

3. Applicant-Zeeshan has approached this Court by way of filing present bail application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 519 of 2020, under Sections 452, 376, 506 IPC, Police Station Karely, District Prayagraj, after rejection of his bail application vide order dated 13.02.2023 passed by Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No. 16, Allahbad.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No. 16, Allahbad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:

4. Victim, a major girl, herself lodged FIR on 09.09.2020 against applicant and co-accused that applicant who is related to her as her real Cousin has committed rape firstly on 24.02.2020 and again on 15.05.2020.
Victim has tried to make complaint against them, however, accused side being powerful persons, had tried to settle the issue.
Even victim has approached the authorities through Jan Sunwai but they have not responded.

5. From record it also revealed that victim has not supported her case in statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. during investigation and it also appears that during investigation Nikah was solemnised between applicant and victim and a written contract was also executed.
Later on the marriage was registered and a certificate in this regard was issued on 31.08.2021.

6. Facts further unfold that meanwhile on the basis of statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. where she has not supported case of prosecution a final report was submitted on 05.11.2020.

After a period of about 17 months victim filed a protest petition alleging that her statements were recorded under pressure and her Nikah and marriage certification proceedings were undertaken by putting her under threat.
7. Magistrate concerned vide order dated 30.04.2022 directed for re-investigation of case.

During re-investigation victim?s statement was again recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. wherein she has supported prosecution case and also stated why she has not narrated correct facts in her earlier statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
8.
Learned counsel for applicant submits that victim is her legally wedded wife as both have solemnised Nikah and marriage has been registered under the provisions of Special Marriage Act.
He further submits that a dispute was arose at the time of Rukhsat as victim has demanded a huge sum of amount, otherwise threatened to implicate him in criminal proceedings.
Both parties have filed litigations, i.e., applicant has filed ?Dawa Rukhsati? and victim has filed ?suit for dissolution of marriage? which are still pending before concerned Court.
Learned counsel submits that all the allegations against applicant are false.

Victim was in consensual relationship with applicant and later on marriage was solemnised, therefore, any allegation of a married wife against applicant, i.e.,
her husband, will fall under marital rape, which is not an offence since victim is a girl of more than 18 years old.

Learned counsel also submits that applicant was never called for any investigation and during re-investigation when police repeatedly raided, he surrendered on 11.01.2023 and since then he is in jail.
9. Above submissions are opposed by learned Brief Holder appearing for State.

He submits that victim has made a categorical statement during re-investigation under Section 164 Cr.P.C. wherein she not only stated about occurrence of rape but circumstances under which she was forced to give a wrong statement during earlier investigation and even before Magistrate.

10. Learned counsel for Informant submits that victim was forced to give an incorrect statement in earlier round of investigation and she has repeatedly approached the authorities concerned with complaint, however, no one has responded positively and since a final report was submitted, she on a legal advise, filed protest petition which has been allowed and order of re-investigation was Zeeshan vs State Of U.P. on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151625182/
2 passed.
Applicant has not challenged the said order before any Court of Law.

During re-investigation victim has specifically stated against applicant in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
11.
In the present case victim, a major girl, has alleged offence of rape on two occasions by applicant.
However, it has also come on record that she has reconciled from her version as stated in FIR while she has given her statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
Further, it has come on record that Nikah was solemnised between parties in presence of family members and even marriage was registered under the provisions of Special Marriage Act.
Applicant and victim have also initiated proceedings against each other.
However, one fact which exist, as on date, is that, victim is wife of applicant atleast since 31.08.2021 when marriage certificate was issued.

12. It is also not disputed that victim has not supported her case during earlier round of investigation and final report was submitted, though during re-investigation in a subsequent statement before Magistrate she has completely supported prosecution case.
Applicant was not arrested during earlier investigation as well as atleast for nine months after the order of re-investigation was passed as he has finally surrendered on 11.01.2023.
During this period subsequent statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded on 24.07.2022, therefore, it cannot be said that in case of bail applicant can now influence victim.
Also taking note that presently victim is a legally wedded wife of applicant, therefore, applicant, who is in jail since 11.01.2023 has made out a case for bail.

13. However, applicant is directed to remain present on each and every date as and when required by Trial Court during trial and in case any application for exemption on vague ground is filed, the same shall be a ground for Trial Court to cancel bail immediately.
14. Let the applicant-Zeeshan be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment or exemption from appearance on the date fixed in trial.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
Zeeshan vs State Of U.P. on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151625182/

3 (iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of applicant,
if there is no other legal impediment.
(v) Trial Court is also directed to record statement of victim in trial within a period of three months from today, if there is no other legal impediment.

15. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by Court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, Court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
16. The bail application is allowed.
17.
It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of adjudicating the present bail application.

Order Date :- 19.5.2023 AK  Zeeshan vs State Of U.P. on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151625182/
